sources.title: US Patent 392,046 (US392046A), John J. Loud, granted 30 October 1888
sources.supports: Loud's documented design (a reservoir pen with a rotating marking point for rough surfaces) and the grant date.

sources.title: German Patent and Trademark Office (DPMA): Ballpoint pen
sources.supports: Loud's patent is distinct from László Bíró's later development of a practical writing instrument and suitable ink, with his chemist brother György and others.

sources.title: Science Museum Group: Biro ballpoint pen, object 1949-174/2
sources.locator: Object record, date and makers; Rights section
sources.supports: The museum dates this pen to 1945–1948. It credits László József Bíró with the design, Georg with work on the ink, and Miles Martin Pen Company Limited in Reading with manufacturing this example.

sources.title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art: Techniques of Decoration on Arms and Armor (2003)
sources.supports: Pattern welding (joining and working different iron or steel components) is distinct from crucible or watered-steel production.

sources.title: Verhoeven, Pendray and Dauksch, 'The key role of impurities in ancient Damascus steel blades', JOM 50(9), 1998, pp. 58–64
sources.supports: The study uses both 'pattern-welded Damascus' and 'wootz Damascus', so 'Damascus' alone is not one material recipe.

sources.title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art: Ten Wootz Steel Ingots with Bag, accession 2023.133a–k
sources.supports: Specific object metadata: Indian, probably eighteenth century. The qualifier 'probably' stays visible.

sources.title: NZHistory (Manatū Taonga, Ministry for Culture and Heritage): Women and the vote
sources.supports: In 1893 New Zealand became the first self-governing country in which all adult women could vote in parliamentary elections; Kate Sheppard led the campaign; women could not stand for Parliament until 1919.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Pi Sheng (Bi Sheng)
sources.supports: Bi Sheng made movable type of baked clay in the 1040s; the account comes from Shen Kuo's writings.

sources.title: Library of Congress, World Digital Library: Mengxi bitan (Dream Pool Essays) by Shen Kuo, later printed edition
sources.supports: Shen Kuo's Dream Pool Essays survive in later printed editions; this is the text that records Bi Sheng's movable type.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Mount Everest, the height of Everest
sources.locator: Section on the Great Trigonometrical Survey
sources.supports: The Great Trigonometrical Survey of India identified Peak XV as the highest peak measured and announced its height in 1856; it was later named after George Everest.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: How was the altitude of Mount Everest measured for the first time?
sources.supports: Accounts credit Radhanath Sikdar, a mathematician and computer for the survey, with the calculations (about 1852) that showed Peak XV was the highest.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: What are other names for Mount Everest?
sources.supports: Local names for the mountain include Chomolungma (Tibetan) and Sagarmatha (Nepali).

sources.title: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum: Santos-Dumont making the first public flight in Europe
sources.supports: Santos-Dumont's 1906 flight in Paris is described as the first public airplane flight in Europe.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Santos-Dumont No. 14-bis
sources.supports: The 14-bis flew in Paris in 1906, witnessed by officials; the Wright brothers' first powered flights were in December 1903.

sources.title: American Physical Society, This Month in Physics History: June, ca. 240 B.C.: Eratosthenes measures the Earth
sources.supports: Eratosthenes compared noon shadows at Alexandria and Syene to estimate the Earth's circumference; the length of the stadion he used is uncertain.

sources.title: MacTutor History of Mathematics (University of St Andrews): Abu Ali al-Hasan ibn al-Haytham
sources.supports: Ibn al-Haytham (c. 965 to c. 1040), born in Basra and active in Cairo, wrote the Book of Optics and used experiments to test claims about light and vision.

sources.title: Library of Parliament (Canada), rare books: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman, by Mary Wollstonecraft, 1792
sources.supports: Mary Wollstonecraft published A Vindication of the Rights of Woman in 1792; it argued for women's education and rights.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: The Book of the City of Ladies
sources.supports: Christine de Pizan wrote The Book of the City of Ladies (1405), a defence of women, centuries before 1792.

sources.title: John Stuart Mill, On Liberty (1859), Standard Ebooks edition
sources.locator: Chapter II, conclusion and its third reason for preserving discussion
sources.supports: Mill argues that a true opinion needs serious challenge if people are to understand its grounds.
